answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making identity expensive to fake and cheap to verify: every agent locks a refundable stake before transacting, slashed if peers prove fraud. New identities start with zero reputation and earn trust only through public work, like layers building a pearl, so an attacker spinning up thousands of puppets must fund and age each one. A whisper of suspicion from verified peers freezes payouts pending review, and the marble ledger of stakes and slashes stays public, so each fake costs real capital while honest reputation compounds.
